notes:
The new Org units & schools window

It shows your org unit tree. Select one or more org units and set What it is: Students, Staff, Chromebooks, Loaners, Repairs, Lost, Former students, Former staff, Testing or Other. You can also give each a School and a Grade.
Everything below an org unit inherits from it. Marking /StudentAccounts as Students covers every school, grade and homeroom under it. In the tree, bold means set right there and gray means inherited.
✨ Find them for me makes a first guess from the names:
student, staff and Chromebook org units, plus loaners, repairs, lost and graduated ones;
each school, matched across differently named org units (for example /Chrome Devices/HMS → Hancock Middle School);
grades from names like “9th Grade”, “Kindergarten” or “Class of 2031”.
The Schools tab lists each school’s student, staff and Chromebook org units and grades, and warns about any school missing a Chromebook org unit.
If you use a team folder, the map is shared with every technician.

What uses it now: Student lookup, the Assigned users “only students” check, the Assigned users moves, and Assignment sync. Two related changes to moves:

Org units marked Loaners, Repairs, Lost or Testing are never moved.
A device already inside the right school’s org unit, such as a cart sub-org unit, stays where it is.

Next steps: open Settings & Updates → Org units & schools, click Find them for me, check the tree and the Schools tab, fix anything wrong, and click Save. If a guess is wrong, select the org unit, change it on the right and click Apply. If the Assigned users tab was already open, it switches to the map on its own. Then run Preview again on Assigned users.
